venue.name: Somenos Marsh Wildlife Society
venue.description: The Somenos Marsh Wildlife Society is a 35 year old charitable society that looks after the S-amunu, or Somenos, Conservation Area just north of Duncan. The conservation area covers 200 hectares of lake, wetland, creeks and Garry oak meadow, and was the first place in British Columbia recognised as an Important Bird and Biodiversity Area, for its wintering Trumpeter Swans and its Great Blue Herons. The society has built the places a group actually visits: the Somenos Marsh Open Air Classroom, with gravel trails, a raised boardwalk, a viewing tower, interpretive signs and a log bench circle, and the Drinkwater Dock on Somenos Lake. It does not run a nature house, and its own office on Station Street in Duncan is open by appointment only. No guided walk, school programme or booked visit is published on the site.

facility_notes.lunch_space: There are picnic tables, and the Peninsula Co-op Talking Circle is available for classes or groups to gather and share knowledge about the area. Both are outdoors.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Flat gravel trails lead to the viewing platform, and the raised Watts Walk boardwalk is level with secure handrails. Getting to the top of the viewing tower means stairs.
facility_notes.bus_parking: There is a parking lot a short distance north on the Trans-Canada Highway just after the Beverly Street intersection. Look for the long brown fence and kiosk, and give plenty of notice that you are turning in. Nothing is said about whether a bus fits.

venue.seasonal_notes: The boardwalk is built high enough to stay usable through winter, when the fields around it flood. The Trumpeter Swans that the marsh is known for arrive in late autumn.

programs.name: Group visit to the Open Air Classroom
programs.description: The Somenos Marsh Open Air Classroom is an outdoor site the society built and maintains, off the S-amunu dike trail beside the Trans-Canada Highway north of Duncan. Flat gravel trails lead to the Cowichan Wheels viewing platform and on up the stairs of a viewing tower, or out along the raised Watts Walk boardwalk over the marsh, which is level and has handrails. Interpretive signs along the boardwalk carry Hul'q'umi'num names and explain the history and the wildlife. There are picnic tables and the Peninsula Co-op Talking Circle, a ring of log benches the site says classes or groups can use. Nothing is booked and no one guides you. There is a donation box near the entrance towards the volunteer upkeep.
programs.what_children_do: Walk flat gravel trails out to a viewing platform, then either climb the tower stairs or follow the raised boardwalk out over the marsh, stopping at signs about the birds and the water. On the boardwalk they can run, because it is level the whole way and fenced with handrails. A group can sit together on the log benches of the Talking Circle.
programs.our_note: There is nothing indoors here and no washroom is mentioned anywhere on the site, so sort both out before you set off. The level boardwalk with handrails is the reason this works for small children, and it stays usable in winter when the fields flood. The turn in off the highway is easy to miss, so slow down early.
programs.practical_summary: Flat gravel trails, a level boardwalk with handrails, picnic tables and a ring of log benches a group can sit on. Washrooms, any shelter from rain and whether a bus can get in are not stated anywhere, so ring first.
programs.extra_fees_note: There is a donation box near the entrance for contributions towards the ongoing volunteer maintenance, any amount helps.
programs.evidence: There are picnic tables, and the Peninsula Co-op Talking Circle is available for classes or groups to gather and share knowledge about the area.

programs.name: Drinkwater Dock visit
programs.description: A second, separate spot on Somenos Lake, at the far end of Drinkwater Road past the BC Forest Discovery Centre. The society built it in 2007 and gifted it, along with the information kiosk, to the Municipality of North Cowichan, and it still maintains the area. It is an elevated walkway out to a floating dock. Nothing is booked and no one guides you, and it is roughly ten minutes drive from the Open Air Classroom rather than part of the same site.
programs.what_children_do: Walk out along a raised walkway onto a floating dock on the lake, look for birds on the water, and fish from the dock if they bring their own gear. Canoes and kayaks are launched from here.
programs.our_note: This is a dock and a walkway, not a trail system, so it is a short stop and works best paired with the marsh site up the road. Children will be right at the edge of open water with no fence, so plan for more adults than you would need on the boardwalk. Nothing is published about a washroom or a car park here.
programs.practical_summary: A short raised walkway out to a floating dock on the lake. Washrooms, parking, shelter and how much of it is step free are not stated, so treat it as an unserviced stop.
programs.evidence: an elevated walkway to a floating dock looking that provides kids fishing opportunities, kayak and canoe launching, and wildlife viewing out on Somenos Lake

images.alt: A raised wooden boardwalk with railings turns a corner and runs out through tall marsh grass and low shrubs, with an orange railed section further along and a wooded hill under grey cloud beyond.
A ring of split log benches resting on tree stumps sits on a flat gravel clearing among young trees, with one person and a wheelbarrow at the far side.

A timber kiosk with a shingled roof stands beside a gravel path holding three illustrated panels under the heading Somenos Marsh Open Air Classroom, one a site map and the others showing a heron, a salmon and waterfowl.
An aerial view of a wide shallow lake ringed by marsh, fields and woodland, with a town and a highway running along the far shore and hills behind.

gaps: No guided walk, school programme, classroom session or booked group visit is published anywhere. Searching their own site for school, education, tour and guided walk turns up only volunteer work parties, past festival events and a mention that school groups already come. If you want someone to meet your group, that has to be arranged directly.

There is no nature house and no visitor centre. The only indoor address is the society office at #3-55 Station St in Duncan, and the site says that is open by appointment only. Everything a group would visit is outdoors and unstaffed.
WASHROOMS: the site never mentions a toilet at the Open Air Classroom or the Drinkwater Dock. Assume there is none until someone tells you otherwise.

PRICE: the site never uses the word free and never prints an admission charge. The Open Air Classroom has a donation box for volunteer upkeep, and the Drinkwater Dock was built by the society and gifted to the Municipality of North Cowichan. Both are recorded here as free on that basis.
No youngest age, group size limit, how many adults to bring, or how far ahead to ring is published for either place.
Nothing is published about shelter from rain, and there is no indoor space. Malcolm's Place, a covered accessible teaching space, is being fundraised for and is not built.
The boardwalk is described as wheelchair accessible and level with handrails. Whether a pushchair works on the gravel trails is not stated, and reaching the top of the viewing tower means stairs.
No opening hours are published for the Open Air Classroom or the dock. The footer has an Hours heading with nothing under it.

The events calendar carries no dates. It points at their Facebook page and at Nature Cowichan instead, and the newest events on their own site are volunteer work parties from 2024 and a family open house from 2021, so anything that looks like a programme here has already passed.
Every photograph on the site carries its file name as its alt text, so all the descriptions here were written after looking at the images.

RETRIEVAL NOTE: this site is Squarespace. The map block that carries the site's coordinates and the search results are both rendered by JavaScript, so a plain fetch shows the page text but no coordinates and no search.

COORDINATES: nothing on their site publishes a point for the office at 55 Station Street. The only map links they have point at the Open Air Classroom and at Drinkwater Dock, which are separate places out in the marsh, and the point we had, 48.78994 and -123.70597, does not match either of them or the office address. It has been cleared because it cannot be traced to anything the site actually publishes. The address stands and the coordinates still need to be worked out from it.

values: Somenos Marsh Open Air Classroom, off the Trans-Canada Highway north of Beverly Street
conflicts.note: Their website gives two different places and they are not the same trip. The Station Street address in Duncan is a small office you can only visit by appointment. The place a group actually goes is the Open Air Classroom out at the marsh, off the Trans-Canada Highway just north of Beverly Street, and that is where the map pin here points. Say which one you mean when you ring.
